_comment: Hand-authored looks built from blocks -- the same building blocks a show
folder's routines are made of (engine/blocks.py). Kept apart from
looks.json because that file is GENERATED by shared/tools/port_library.py
and guarded as a reproducible artifact: test_qlc_parity.py asserts every
entry in it matches a function in despacio.qxw, and the porter would
erase anything hand-added. The library the console sees is the two merged.
Not a show-folder routine. A routine is a timed, multi-row document a
timeline plays; one of these is a single block, picked live from the
console and turned by hand.
A look names a block and its arguments. Everything the console shows for
it -- the sliders, their ranges, the sentences under them -- comes from the
block's own declarations in blocks.PARAMS, so nothing here describes a
control. An argument left out takes the block's declared default.
Movement looks set 'spread' explicitly. The orbit block's own default
spreads the heads a whole cycle apart; these were authored moving
together, with the console's Spread macro there to open them up.
Two ways a parametric look can stand in for a ported one, and the
difference is whether the replacement is EXACT:
'supersedes': true on a look takes over the ported look of the same name,
in place -- the button, its position in the picker and every cue that
names it are unchanged, but it is now a block and can be turned. Only for
exact replacements: test_library measures each against the ported
original on every head, under the shape macros, to a hundredth of a
degree. The positions below are all of this kind.
The 'retired' list HIDES an approximately-replaced ported entry from the
picker. It never deletes it: looks.json's round-trip proof depends on
every entry staying in it, and an operator who wants the original back
is one toggle away.

looks.name: Heads - Ball
looks.notes: Every head on its own calibrated ball point -- the base everything else is an offset from.

looks.name: Heads - Apex
looks.notes: Lifted off the ball towards the apex.

looks.name: Heads - Zenith
looks.notes: Straight up and just over the top -- 92.8 degrees, past the old +-90 centre limit, and reachable because in this mount the elevation channel is the 540-degree pan.

looks.name: Heads - Floor
looks.notes: Dropped onto the floor round the ball. The ported heads differed by a thousandth of a degree; this is their mean.

looks.name: Heads - Crowd
looks.notes: Straight down. The safety taper decides how bright that is allowed to be, after everything, as it always did.

looks.name: Heads - Circle
looks.notes: Swung 45 degrees round, just above level.

looks.name: Heads - Wall Graze
looks.notes: Swung 45 degrees round, level -- skimming the walls.

looks.name: Heads - Walls
looks.notes: Turned all the way round onto the walls. 180.35 degrees, which the old +-180 centre limit refused; these heads reach 198.

looks.name: Heads - Cathedral
looks.notes: Turned round and lifted -- the cathedral.

looks.name: Ball Orbit
looks.notes: The plain circle around each head's own calibrated ball aim. Size and Centre turn this one entry into most of the Ball family.

looks.name: Lazy Orbit
looks.notes: The ported 'Lazy Circle', as a block: four heads a quarter-cycle apart on a slow ring. shared/tools/audit_library.py fits it within 1.6 degrees RMS (2.2 worst, about one 8-bit pan step) of the eight stored steps it replaces -- and unlike them, its radius, flattening and speed can be turned.

looks.name: Wide Sweep
looks.notes: The same orbit flattened into a horizontal oval. On a corner rig this reads as a sweep rather than a circle -- there is far more bearing available than elevation.

looks.name: Slow Pendulum
looks.notes: Across the room and back, easing to a stop at each end. Put Spread on it and the four heads pass each other.

looks.name: Nod
looks.notes: Vertical. Small on purpose: the taper is doing work every time these point down, and a big nod spends the whole look dimmed.

looks.name: Figure Eight
looks.notes: Crosses its own middle twice a cycle. Nothing in the ported library does this -- a chaser would have needed eight stored steps and would still have stepped between them.

looks.name: Wind Out
looks.notes: Winds out from the ball and resets. A build look.

looks.name: Converge
looks.notes: The same curve read backwards, so the four beams close onto the ball together. Lands well on a drop.

looks.name: Drift
looks.notes: Each head wanders its own way. Random-looking and reproducible: the same seed gives the same show on the rig, in the plan view and in previz.

looks.name: Restless
looks.notes: The same block with more stops and no easing. Twitchy rather than drifting.

looks.name: Slow Breathe
looks.notes: A symmetrical swell with no attack. A MULTIPLIER, like every level look, so it dims whatever color and route are running rather than replacing them.

looks.name: Rolling Breathe
looks.notes: The same swell spread evenly across the heads, so it travels round the room instead of pumping as one lamp.

looks.name: Heartbeat
looks.notes: Falls from full each bar.

looks.name: Runner
looks.notes: A bump of brightness travelling across the heads. Narrow enough to light roughly one at a time; widen it and they overlap into a wave.

looks.name: Pin Runner
looks.notes: The same block scoped to the pinspots. On two fixtures it is an alternation.

looks.name: Color Drift Parametric
looks.notes: Drifts out within a family and back rather than round the whole wheel. A small span over many bars is what reads as 'the room is slowly changing' instead of as a rainbow.

looks.name: Rainbow Roll
looks.notes: The whole wheel, with each head a quarter turn behind the last.

looks.name: Pin Drift Slow
looks.notes: Warm pastels crawling. What the ported Pin Drift does across twelve stored steps, as four numbers.

looks.name: Duo Pink/Cyan
looks.notes: Alternating across the heads, so on four corners the two colors land diagonally opposite and read across the room.

looks.name: Duo Swap
looks.notes: The same pair trading places over the cycle. There is no way to express this as a stored scene -- it is two scenes and the road between them.

retired.name: Lazy Circle
retired.note: orbit(radius 18.75, elongation 0.925, spread 1) within 1.6 degrees RMS -- the one ported path the audit found a block for. Still in looks.json and still selectable from the picker's 'retired' toggle.
